subject: [PATCH 1/9] memcg: make the v1 soft limit knob inert

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton questioned whether the recent syzbot report was a new issue or a previously existing problem that has only recently been exposed, and suggested considering backporting the fix.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks, I'll pluck this one as a hotfix.

It's old code, yes?  Are there any theories about why the sysbot issue
has just popped up?  Should we backport the fix?

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the patch's behavior of ignoring writes to memory.soft_limit_in_bytes is intentional, but noted that the reproducer's test case toggling MGLRU on and off continuously is not recommended.
reviews.raw_body:
The reproducer is toggling MGLRU on and off continuosly which is not really
recommended.

2026-08-12.patch_summary: This patch makes the v1 soft limit knob inert by ignoring writes to it and always returning its maximum value on read. The knob has been deprecated since Linux version 6.12, but was still being used in some cases. This change ensures that the knob behaves consistently everywhere, including PREEMPT_RT systems where soft limit reclaim is disabled. Additionally, this patch fixes a syzbot report related to memory pressure notification and removes references to the soft limit from documentation.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the soft limit knob is deprecated and has no effect, but expressed willingness to consider alternative behavior (EOPNOTSUPP) if reviewer prefers.
reviews.raw_body:
I followed the memory.kmem.limit_in_bytes example. If you have strong opinion, I
am ok with EOPNOTSUPP as well.
